title: Graph Neural Networks for Influence Maximization in Social Networks: An Unsupervised Minimum Dominating Set Approach
abstract: arXiv:2609.13836v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The Minimum Dominating Set (MDS) problem is a classic NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem with critical applications in social network analysis, including viral marketing, influence maximization, public health interventions, and information dissemination. Identifying a minimal set of influential individuals whose reach covers an entire social network is central to these applications, yet remains computationally challenging at scale. Graph neural networks (GNNs) have emerged as powerful tools for learning over graphs, and recent work explores their application to hard combinatorial problems. This paper presents a novel unsupervised GNN framework for the MDS problem that eliminates the need for ground-truth solutions during training. Trained on 12,000 synthetic graphs with diverse structural properties, our method achieves up to 55x faster inference than metaheuristic baselines and up to 14x faster inference than supervised learning

translated_title: 基于图神经网络的社交网络影响力最大化：一种无监督最小支配集方法
translated_abstract: 最小支配集（MDS）问题是一个经典的NP难组合优化问题，在社交网络分析中具有关键应用，包括病毒式营销、影响力最大化、公共卫生干预和信息传播。识别出一组能覆盖整个社交网络的最小规模有影响力个体集合是这些应用的核心，然而在大规模场景下仍然面临计算挑战。图神经网络（GNN）已成为图学习领域的强大工具，近期的研究工作探索了其在困难组合问题上的应用。本文提出了一种新颖的用于MDS问题的无监督GNN框架，该框架在训练过程中无需真实解标注。在12,000个具有多样化结构特性的合成图上训练后，我们的方法相比元启发式基线方法推理速度快达55倍，相比监督学习方法推理速度快达14倍。
tldr: 本文提出一种无需真实解标注的无监督图神经网络框架来解决最小支配集问题，在社交网络影响力最大化应用中相比元启发式基线方法推理速度快达55倍。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an unsupervised GNN framework for the Minimum Dominating Set problem that eliminates the need for ground-truth solutions during training, achieving up to 55x faster inference than metaheuristic baselines for influence maximization in social networks.
